plot: At the first dinner in the new house Grandma's borrowed folding table tips every time Dad leans, sliding Mia's milk and Grandma's first soup toward the edge; Zeek blames a sloping floor and his napkin fix tips it the other way while Crispy holds the soup, until Bup, under the table, finds the real cause — the leg Dad never clicked (seen in the opening) — and — the twist — the hinge can only lock with no weight on it, so Lolly rings a spoon on Mia's glass, Mia calls a standing toast for Grandma, and Zeek clicks the leg shut; then Grandma announces she'll plant her petunias tomorrow in 'that ugly old black pot'.

script.title: Can Zeek Hold Up the Dinner Table?

beats.say: The table is tilting! Four degrees and climbing!
Everybody to the high side of the basket! Go!
First dinner in the new house. On Grandma's old folding table.
Every time Dad leans on his elbow, the whole table tips.
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
And Mr. Pot is somewhere in this house. Somewhere!
One problem at a time, Pim. Table first.
In the middle of the table: Grandma's soup. Her first soup here.
She hummed the whole time she cooked it. I listened.
Then this dinner is perfect. Nobody spills anything.
Earlier, Dad unfolded the table. One leg didn't click. He shrugged.
Dad leans again. Mia's milk slides an inch toward the edge.
The milk is walking! Somebody stop the milk!
My calculations say it's the floor. The floor slopes toward Dad.
Zeek rolls a pea. It rolls toward Dad. Then it stops.
See? Science. We just lift Dad's side a little bit.
Bup and Pim drag a folded napkin under Dad's table leg.
Dad leans. The table tips the other way. Toward Grandma.
The soup is three inches from the edge! Three!
Hot soup. Grandma's lap. Right there!
Crispy leans on the soup bowl. Holding it back.
Hold it as long as you need. Warm is my thing.
But my numbers... the floor... the pea...
Bup climbs down under the table. It's dark. Shoes everywhere.
Dad's sock. Mia's sneaker. Grandma's slippers. Phew.
Then Bup sees it. One table leg. Its metal knee is bent.
Zeek! It's not the floor! This leg never clicked!
A loose hinge! That's why the pea stopped. The tilt kept changing!
To lock it, someone must push the hinge until it clicks.
That someone is me. I know exactly where the lock is.
Zeek has never pushed anything heavier than a pencil.
He pushes. Nothing. The whole family is leaning on the table.
It won't move while they lean on it. Impossible!
Above them, Dad puts his elbow down. Hard.
If that leg folds, everything comes down. Soup, milk, us!
They all have to stop leaning. All at the same time!
How do you make a whole family stand up at once?
Easy. Mia loves a toast. Watch this.
Lolly taps a spoon on Mia's glass. Ting. Ting. Ting.
Mia jumps up. 'A toast! Everybody stand up for Grandma!'
Chairs scrape. Everyone stands. Nobody leans. The table is light.
Now!
Zeek pushes with everything. Glasses crooked. Eyes shut.
The leg locks. The table stands flat. Perfectly flat.
Grandma raises her glass. 'To the new house. And this table.'
My calculations were completely wrong. I've never been happier.
You pushed something heavier than a pencil, Zeek.
And the soup survived. Listen. She's humming again.
Then Grandma says one more thing.
'Tomorrow I plant my petunias. In that ugly old black pot.'
Ugly old black pot? Three eyes? That pot?!
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
